## Review

**8 out of 10, Strong.** Presentation quality, judged with the SlideDeck Co review heuristic (https://slidedeck.co/review-methodology/). The ask, the evidence and the merit of the idea are not rated.

The deck has a clear, disciplined system: serif action titles with a one-line subtitle that states the point, a single red highlight against grey and charcoal, and sourced charts with direct labels. It reads as an argument, with slides 28 to 30 building one stacked bar step by step and slides 65 to 67 reusing a single consumer-spending bar to frame two eras. Defects are real but modest: the two-column bars on slide 12 have low-contrast white labels on pale pink and light grey, many charts leave large empty margins with tiny legends, and the circle slides (2, 10, 13, 15, 18) carry little visual information. I only saw 72 of 134 pages, so the later China and regulation sections are unjudged.

**Worth keeping:** Keep the action-title plus subtitle pattern, the red-for-the-point colour logic, the sourced footers, and the incremental chart builds on slides 28 to 30.

**Most useful repair:** Raise contrast of white labels on pale fills (slides 8, 12, 45, 65), and enlarge the small legends and axis text on slides like 5, 6 and 9.

**What would change the score:** Replace some of the repeated circle-and-arrow slides and the near-empty divider slides with a bolder visual device, and fill the wide chart margins so the data sits larger.

_Confidence medium. 72 of 134 pages inspected on contact sheets, 4 at readable size. Reviewed Reviewed 2026-11-08. Model-assisted review (claude-sonnet-5-5)._

## Summary

The deck opens with a title slide and a 2021 agenda built around four themes: COVID acceleration, the great unbundling, harder problems including China, and tech becoming a regulated industry. The first section shows how the pandemic pulled forward years of adoption, using charts on labour force change, ecommerce share, online grocery, video calls and working from home. The middle sections examine how retail, logistics and advertising are being split apart, with Amazon, Shopify, Nike, streaming services and cookie-based targeting as recurring examples. A longer section on harder problems covers electric vehicles, renewable energy costs, SpaceX and machine learning. It is followed by a section on China's technology supply chain, its internet market, and the growth of India and other markets. The deck closes with a regulation section and a conclusion comparing the first and second fifty years of technology, ending on a thank-you slide. Slides 3, 10 and 42 use section dividers with a single headline, and slide 12 pairs two stacked bars to make a point about business travel.

## Questions about this deck

**What does the Benedict Evans deck say about Amazon's revenue growth?**

Slide 27 says Amazon's revenue grew 37% in 2020, shown on a line chart of Amazon annual revenue in $bn from 1995 to 2020.

**What share of US parcel deliveries does the Benedict Evans deck say Amazon handles?**

Slide 23 says a third of all US parcels are now delivered by Amazon's own logistics network. The source is ShipMatrix, using US parcel deliveries for July 2020.

**What topics are listed in the agenda of the Benedict Evans deck?**

Slide 2 lists COVID acceleration, The Great Unbundling, Harder problems, China, and Tech becomes a regulated industry as the agenda for 2021.

**What does the Benedict Evans deck say about Shopify's GMV?**

Slide 33 says Shopify has come from nowhere to over $100bn of GMV in 2020, shown on a bar chart of Shopify GMV in $bn.

**Layout**

Two-band frame: a light grey header band occupies the top 20.5% of the slide and a light grey footer band the bottom 13.9%, with a white body panel between them. The title and subtitle are left-aligned at x 20.1% in the header, the chart runs from about x 17.5% to 95% in the body with a legend at the far left (x 4.8%), and the footer holds the source and footnote at x 20.5% plus the byline, date and page number on the right, ending at x 95.6%.

**Visuals**

One line chart titled 'Ecommerce as a share of addressable retail*', with a y-axis from 0% to 40% in 10% steps (dotted horizontal gridlines at each step) and an x-axis from 2010 to 2021 with year labels. Series 1, 'UK (monthly)', red line: about 6.5% at start of 2010, about 8% in 2011, about 10% in 2013, about 12% in 2015, about 16% in 2016, about 19% in 2019, about 20% at start of 2020, a sharp rise to about 34% around mid-2020 (highlighted peak), a fall to about 28% late 2020, a rise to about 31% at end of 2020, ending about 30%. Series 2, 'USA (quarterly)', dark grey line: about 6% in 2010, about 10% in 2015, about 17% in early 2020 (flat), a rise to about 22% around mid-2020 (highlighted peak), ending about 20.5%. Values are estimates, not printed on the slide. Legend at top-left: red short line with 'UK (monthly)' above dark grey short line with 'USA (quarterly)'. No data labels, no other highlighted points. Axis baseline is a thin grey line at 0%.

**Design**

Background light grey #F1F1F1 for the header and footer bands, white #FFFFFF body panel. Titles in a serif (Photina-like, regular weight) #545454; subtitle serif regular #545454; chart title and labels in Helvetica Neue sans-serif, chart title bold #545554; body and axis text regular #545454 to #535353; byline bold Helvetica Neue #A6A6A6 with date and page number regular #A6A6A6. Title text about 5.6% of slide height, subtitle about 2.6%, body and labels about 1.9%. Chart series lines about 0.3% of slide height thick: UK red #E8483B, USA dark grey #4A4A4A. Gridlines dotted light grey #BEBEBE. No shadows, gradients or rounded corners.

**Layout**

Two-band slide: a light grey header band (top about 20% of the height) holds the title and subtitle, left-aligned at x 20.1%, with the title sitting above the subtitle. Below it a white content area holds a full-width stacked column chart starting at x about 19% with a chart title above the plot and a legend at the far left (x 3%) level with the top of the plot. A grey footer band (bottom about 14%) holds the source note and footnote left-aligned at x 20.5%, and the author, date and page number right-hand side of the footer, with the page number at x 95%.

**Visuals**

Stacked column chart. Title: 'UK retail sales* excluding grocery (average weekly by month, £bn)', bold sans, dark grey. Y-axis: £bn, linear, range 0 to 5, labelled ticks 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, with faint dotted horizontal gridlines at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 and a solid thin axis line at 0. X-axis: time in months from 2010 to 2020 (about 130 monthly columns), labelled at each January 2010, 2011 ... 2020. Series: Offline (dark grey, top segment) and Online (red, bottom segment), stacked. No printed data values. Estimates: 2010 monthly totals about 2.8 to 3.1 with Online about 0.3; 2014 totals about 3.4 to 3.6 with Online about 0.6; 2016 totals about 3.6 to 3.7 with Online about 0.8; 2018 totals about 4.0 to 4.1 with Online about 1.1; 2019 totals about 4.3 to 4.4 with Online about 1.3; early 2020 Online about 1.5 to 1.4 and total dips to about 3.7 (Feb) then about 2.8 (Apr 2020) with Online about 1.6; mid 2020 totals rise to about 4.8 to 4.9 with Online peaking about 2.1 (late 2020); final bar about 4.6 total with Online about 2.0. Legend: two entries, Offline (dark grey square) above Online (red square), no border. No highlighted points beyond the 2020 spike.

**Design**

Background: Solid light grey #F1F1F1 covering the whole slide, with a white #FFFFFF band from y 20.5% to 86% carrying the chart. Flat, minimal consultancy style. Background light grey #F1F1F1 in the header and footer bands, with a white #FFFFFF content band between them. Title in light serif (Photina), dark grey #545454, large. Subtitle in the same serif, dark grey #545454, smaller. Chart title and axis labels in Helvetica Neue (bold for chart title, regular for ticks), dark grey #545454 and #535353. Bars: Offline dark grey #4D4D4D, Online red #E8443A. Gridlines light grey dotted #BFBFBF. Footer credit in Helvetica Neue Bold #A6A6A6 for name, regular #A6A6A6 for date and page number. Title about 5.6% of slide height, subtitle and chart title about 2.6% and 2.2%, body and axis text about 1.85%. Square corners, no shadows, no gradients.

### Slide 7

**Text**

Online grocery sales have doubled / Forced adoption, forced experiment / UK online grocery as % total grocery / 15% / 10% / 5% / 0% / 2010 / 2011 / 2012 / 2013 / 2014 / 2015 / 2016 / 2017 / 2018 / 2019 / 2020 / Source: ONS / Benedict Evans / –– January 2021 / 7

**Layout**

Full-slide light grey (#F1F1F1) field with a grey header band at top and a grey footer band at bottom, framing a white content panel between them. The title sits top-left at x 20.1% with the subtitle directly beneath it, both left-aligned on the same left edge. A single line chart fills the white panel, with its chart title left-aligned at x 20.5% above the plot; the source line sits bottom-left at x 20.5% and the footer credit, date and page number sit bottom-right in the grey footer band, the page number at x 95% at the right margin.

**Visuals**

Line chart. Title: 'UK online grocery as % total grocery' (bold sans, dark grey). Y-axis: percentage of total grocery, range 0% to 15%, labelled ticks at 0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, with light dotted horizontal gridlines at 5%, 10% and 15%. X-axis: years 2010 to 2020 labelled at each January, with a thin solid grey baseline at 0%; the series runs monthly to late 2020. Single series, drawn as a red line about 0.5% of slide height thick, colour about #E8453C. Labelled values: none printed on the slide. Estimated values (about): starts at about 2.5% in early 2010; about 3% through 2011 to 2012; about 3.5% in 2013; about 4% in early 2015; about 4.5% in 2016; about 5% through 2017 to 2019; dips to about 5% in early 2020; spikes to about 9.5% in spring 2020; peaks at about 11.1% around mid 2020; falls to about 10.3% in autumn 2020; ends at about 11% at the last point. Legend: none. Highlighted points: none marked, though the 2020 spike is the steepest feature of the line. No photographs, logos or icons.

**Design**

Background: Solid light grey #F1F1F1 covering the whole slide, with a white #FFFFFF panel from y 20.5% to 86.1%. Flat, minimal, editorial look. Background light grey #F1F1F1 in the header and footer bands, white #FFFFFF content panel. Title colour #545454 in a high-contrast book serif (Photina, a Times-like serif), regular weight, about 5.6% of slide height (cap height about 3.9%). Subtitle in the same serif, #545454, about 2.6% of slide height. Chart title and axis labels in a neutral Helvetica-style sans-serif: chart title bold #545554 about 2.2%; tick labels regular #545554 about 1.85%. Source line and footer in Helvetica Neue regular #545454 and #A6A6A6, about 1.85%; footer name bold #A6A6A6. Accent colour: red line #E8453C. Gridlines are thin dotted light grey, about #BBBBBB, 0.1% of slide height. Baseline is a thin solid grey line #888888. No shadows, gradients, rounded corners or borders.

### Slide 8

**Review notes**

- Suggested repair: Raise contrast of white labels on pale fills (slides 8, 12, 45, 65), and enlarge the small legends and axis text on slides like 5, 6 and 9.

**Text**

Forced experiment, forced adoption / Breaking habits - everyone is forced to try things for the first time / Growth of grocery delivery during Covid / Using more / Used for first time / 50% / 40% / 30% / 20% / 10% / 0% / China / UK / USA / Italy / France / Spain / Germany / Brazil / Mexico / Argentina / Source: McKinsey / Benedict Evans / —January 2021 / 8

**Layout**

Full-width two-band slide: a light grey header band (top about 20% of the slide) holds the title and subtitle left-aligned at x 20.1%, and a light grey footer band (bottom about 14%) holds the source line at left and the author, date and page number at right. The white content band between them holds a chart with its title at x 20.5% and y 27.4%, a legend at the far left at x 3.2%, and the vertical bar chart spanning roughly x 20.6% to 95.4%. Text is left-aligned to a common left edge near x 20%; the page number sits at the right margin near x 95%.

**Visuals**

Chart: stacked vertical bar chart titled 'Growth of grocery delivery during Covid'. Y axis is percentage of the population, 0% to 50%, with labelled ticks at 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40% and 50% and dotted light grey horizontal gridlines at each labelled tick; the 0% baseline is a solid grey line. X axis: categories China, UK, USA, Italy, France, Spain, Germany, Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, left to right. Two stacked series per bar: bottom series 'Used for first time' in red, top series 'Using more' in light pink, stacked to a total. The slide prints no data values, so all values are estimates: China about 13 (used for first time) and about 46 total (using more about 33); UK about 11 and about 33 (using more about 22); USA about 10 and about 26 (about 16); Italy about 9 and about 25 (about 16); France about 8 and about 16 (about 8); Spain about 5 and about 15 (about 10); Germany about 3 and about 11 (about 8); Brazil about 11 and about 22 (about 11); Mexico about 9 and about 26 (about 17); Argentina about 6 and about 28 (about 22). Legend: top-left, two square swatches stacked vertically: light pink square labelled 'Using more' above a red square labelled 'Used for first time'. No highlighted points. Bars are narrow, about 3% of slide width, with thin white separators between stacked segments.

**Design**

Background: Light grey #F1F1F1 covering the whole slide, with a white #FFFFFF band behind the chart area (from about 20.5% to 86.1% of slide height). Clean minimal corporate style. Header and footer bands are light grey #F1F1F1 and the central content band is white #FFFFFF. Title is set in a light serif (Photina-like) at regular weight in dark grey #545454, large (about 5.6% of slide height for cap-height text). Subtitle is the same serif in regular weight, about 2.6% of slide height, colour #545454. Chart title and category/axis labels use a sans-serif (Helvetica Neue style); chart title is bold #545554 at about 2.2% of slide height; axis labels and legend labels are regular #545454 or #535353 at about 1.85% of slide height. Accent colours: bars red #EC4A3F for used for first time and light pink #FBDAD9 for using more. Footer text: author name bold in light grey #A6A6A6, date and page number regular #A6A6A6, source line regular #545454, all about 1.85% of slide height. Lines: gridlines are fine dotted mid-grey, about 1px; baseline is a solid grey line. No shadows, gradients, rounded corners or icons.

The page number 9 sits at the far right at x 95%.

**Visuals**

Chart: clustered vertical bar chart titled 'UK adults making personal video calls at least weekly' (bold sans-serif, above the plot). Y-axis: percentage of UK adults, range 0% to 75%, labelled at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% with dotted light grey horizontal gridlines at 25%, 50% and 75%. X-axis: nine platform categories, left to right: Any, WhatsApp, FB Messenger, Facetime, Zoom, Skype, Instagram, Snapchat, MSFT Teams, Houseparty (ten categories in total). Two series: February 2020 in dark grey #535353 (left bar of each pair) and May 2020 in red #EB483F (right bar of each pair). Values are not printed on the slide; estimates from bar heights are: Any Feb about 35%, May about 71%; WhatsApp Feb about 20%, May about 49%; FB Messenger Feb about 18%, May about 41%; Facetime Feb about 13%, May about 30%; Zoom Feb none shown (no bar), May about 23%; Skype Feb about 7%, May about 15%; Instagram Feb about 6%, May about 15%; Snapchat Feb about 6%, May about 10%; MSFT Teams Feb none shown, May about 10%; Houseparty Feb none shown, May about 7%. Legend: top-left of the chart, two square swatches with labels, February 2020 (dark grey #535353) above May 2020 (red #EB483F). No bars are highlighted beyond the colour coding. No photographs, icons or logos.

**Design**

Header and footer bands are light grey #F1F1F1 with the white middle band #FFFFFF; no borders, shadows or gradients. Title in a regular-weight serif (Photina-like) in charcoal #545454. Subtitle in the same serif, regular, #545454. Chart title and all axis, category and legend text in a regular-weight Helvetica Neue-style sans-serif, #545554 or #535353. The author name is bold sans-serif #A6A6A6, the date and page number regular sans-serif #A6A6A6. Source line regular sans-serif #545454. Title text is about 5.6% of slide height, subtitle about 2.6%, chart title about 2.2%, chart labels and footer about 1.9%. Accent colour is red #EB483F for the May 2020 series. Bars are solid fills with thin white separation; gridlines are thin dotted light grey; the category axis is a thin solid grey line.

Line chart titled 'Employment in New York City (000s)'. Y axis: employment in thousands, range 0 to 400, gridlines and labels at 0, 100, 200, 300, 400, dotted light grey horizontal gridlines. X axis: years 1990 to about 2021 with labels at 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020, solid grey baseline. Series: Retail (red #E8443A line) starts about 268 in 1990, dips to about 228 in 1993, rises to about 285 in 2001, falls to about 265 in 2002, rises to about 357 in 2015, stays near 350 through 2019, then drops sharply to about 253 in 2020 before recovering to about 305 at the end. Restaurants & bars (dark grey #545454) starts about 144 in 1990, falls to about 119 in 1993, rises to about 166 in 2001, about 200 in 2008, about 320 in 2018, then plunges to about 90 in 2020 before recovering to about 193 at the end. Clothing stores (light red-pink #F4A09A) starts about 41 in 1990, about 35 in 1993, about 52 in 2001, about 62 in 2013, about 58 in 2018, then falls to about 17 in 2020 and about 24 at the end. Legend at left top of chart: red line Retail, dark grey line Restaurants & bars, pink line Clothing stores. No highlighted points.

### Slide 12

**Review notes**

- Worth studying: Two stacked bars with matching categories let the reader compare frequency and length of business travel side by side.
- Review: Defects are real but modest: the two-column bars on slide 12 have low-contrast white labels on pale pink and light grey, many charts leave large empty margins with tiny legends, and the circle slides (2, 10, 13, 15, 18) carry little visual information.
- Suggested repair: Raise contrast of white labels on pale fills (slides 8, 12, 45, 65), and enlarge the small legends and axis text on slides like 5, 6 and 9.

**Layout**

Full-width title block in a light grey band across the top, with the title and subtitle left-aligned at about x 20% and sitting in the upper third. A white chart panel fills the middle band with a grey footer band below holding the source line at left and the author, date and page number right-aligned at the bottom. Two stacked-column bars sit on a shared baseline, with the chart title left-aligned above the plot area.

**Visuals**

Stacked column chart, titled 'Business travel volume, 2018'. Y-axis from 0% to 100% in 25% steps, with light dotted horizontal gridlines at 25%, 50%, 75% and 100%. X-axis categories: 'Frequency' and 'Length', with a solid thin grey baseline at 0%. Frequency column (about 100% total), bottom to top: 'Every week' about 14% (#EB483F red), 'Every month' about 23% (#F5A39F light red), 'Quarterly' about 36% (#7F7F7F dark grey), 'Less often' about 27% (#A6A6A6 light grey). Length column (about 100% total), bottom to top: '1 Night' about 12% (#EB483F red), '2 Nights' about 39% (#F5A39F light red), '3 Nights' about 31% (#7F7F7F dark grey), 'Longer' about 18% (#A6A6A6 light grey). Segments are separated by thin white lines; labels are white centred inside each segment. No legend; the segment labels act as the legend. No highlighted points. Bars are about 15% of slide width each, with the Frequency bar centred near x 39% and the Length bar near x 76%.

**Design**

Background: Light grey #F1F1F1 band top and bottom, white #FFFFFF chart panel in the middle.

### Slide 28

**Review notes**

- Review: It reads as an argument, with slides 28 to 30 building one stacked bar step by step and slides 65 to 67 reusing a single consumer-spending bar to frame two eras.
- Worth keeping: Keep the action-title plus subtitle pattern, the red-for-the-point colour logic, the sourced footers, and the incremental chart builds on slides 28 to 30.

**Text**

Ecommerce as logistics / What’s Amazon’s market? / US retail revenue by delivery model, 2019 ($bn) / 3,000 / 2,500 / 2,000 / 1,500 / 1,000 / 500 / Ecommerce / 0 / Could be parcels / Could be custom delivered or collected / Source: US Census / Benedict Evans / —— January 2021 / 28

**Layout**

Two-band layout: a light grey header band across the top holding the title and subtitle left-aligned at x≈20%, a white middle band holding a two-bar stacked column chart with its chart title at top-left (x≈20.5%) and y-axis labels at left, and a light grey footer band with the source line at left (x≈20.5%) and the author, date and slide number at right. The left margin is about 20% of the slide width and the right margin about 5%; the white band runs from y≈20.5% to y≈86.1%. The slide number 28 sits at the far right of the footer at x≈94.4%.

**Visuals**

Stacked column chart. Title: 'US retail revenue by delivery model, 2019 ($bn)'. Y-axis: $bn, linear scale from 0 to 3,000 with labelled gridlines at 0, 500, 1,000, 1,500, 2,000, 2,500 and 3,000; gridlines are light grey dotted horizontal lines. X-axis: two categories, 'Could be parcels' and 'Could be custom delivered or collected', with a thin grey baseline at 0. Series: 'Ecommerce' (red #EB483F, bottom segment) and an unlabelled dark grey #535353 upper segment (the rest of the total). Bar 1 'Could be parcels': total about 2,650 (top about 2,650 on the axis, estimated), Ecommerce segment top about 550 (estimated; the bar top is about 2,650 and the red segment ends near 550), dark grey segment about 2,100 (estimated). Bar 2 'Could be custom delivered or collected': total about 1,800 (estimated), Ecommerce segment about 50 (estimated, thin red strip at the base), dark grey segment about 1,750 (estimated). The label 'Ecommerce' is printed in white inside the red segment of bar 1. No legend is printed. Bars are solid rectangles with a thin white separator line between the red and grey segments. No highlighted points.

**Design**

Background light grey #F1F1F1 for header and footer bands, with a white #FFFFFF middle band. Title in PhotinaMT regular serif, colour #545454, about 5.6% of slide height for the title's capital letters, roughly cap height 5.6%. Subtitle in PhotinaMT regular serif, #545454, about 2.6% of slide height. Chart title in HelveticaNeue Bold sans-serif, #545554, about 2.2% of slide height. Axis labels and category labels in HelveticaNeue regular sans-serif, #545554, about 1.85% of slide height. Source line in HelveticaNeue regular, #545454. Footer author name in HelveticaNeue Bold #A6A6A6, date and slide number in HelveticaNeue regular #A6A6A6, all about 1.85% of slide height. Accent colour red #EB483F for the Ecommerce series; main series grey #535353. Gridlines light grey dotted. Bars have square corners, no shadows, no gradients.

Stacked column chart, titled 'US retail revenue by delivery model, 2019 ($bn)'. Y-axis: $bn, range 0 to 3,000, gridlines dotted every 500 at 0, 500, 1,000, 1,500, 2,000, 2,500, 3,000. **Visuals**

Stacked column chart titled 'US online product search by channel'. Y-axis: percentage of US online product search, 0% to 100%, gridlines dotted at 25% intervals, labels 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%. X-axis categories: 'Before lockdown' and 'During lockdown'. Series stacked bottom to top: Other (red #EB483F), Amazon (dark grey #535353), Google (light grey #A7A7A7). During lockdown: Other about 37%, Amazon about 42% (from about 37% to about 79%), Google about 21% (from about 79% to 100%). Values are estimates; the slide prints no data values. **Layout**

Full-slide light grey (#F1F1F1) field with a white band across the middle (about 20.5% to 86% of the height). **Visuals**

Chart: line chart, titled Relative search interest, UK. Y axis: relative search interest, unitless index, range 0 to 125, gridlines and labels at 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 and 125, dotted light grey gridlines. X axis: years 2004 to 2021, one label per year, monthly data points. Series 1, Best (red line, about #E8443A): starts about 28 in early 2004, stays about 25 to 35 until about 2010, rises to about 53 in early 2011, about 70 in 2013, about 85 in 2016, about 90 in 2018, peaks at about 100 in 2020 and ends at about 97 in early 2021. Series 2, Cheap (dark grey line, about #4D4D4D): starts about 63 in 2004, peaks about 74 in late 2004, falls to about 30 to 40 by 2009 with a dip about 23 in early 2011, about 30 by 2014, about 25 in 2017, about 20 in 2019, dips to about 17 in 2020 and ends about 16 in early 2021. Legend: at top left of chart, red line marker labelled Best above dark grey line marker labelled Cheap. No highlighted points. Chart title and axis labels are the only text besides legend.

### Slide 37

**Text**

**Layout**

Two-band slide: a light grey (#F1F1F1) header band across the top holds the title and subtitle, left-aligned at about 20% of slide width; a white chart band fills the middle (about 20.5% to 86% of slide height) with a bar chart, and the same grey band forms the footer at the bottom. The chart title sits at the top-left of the chart area, aligned with the title's left edge only roughly; the source line sits at bottom-left, and the presenter name, date and slide number sit at bottom-right, with the page number flush to the right margin at about 94.4% of width.

**Visuals**

Bar chart (vertical, single series, red bars). Title: 'Mall penetration (GLA per 1000 people)'. Y-axis: 0 to 2,500 with labelled gridlines at 0, 500, 1,000, 1,500, 2,000 and 2,500 (unit: GLA per 1000 people); faint grey dotted horizontal gridlines at each labelled value; no axis title. X-axis: categories USA, Canada, Australia, UK, Chile, Mexico, Brazil, with a thin grey baseline at 0. Series values are not printed; approximate values read from bar heights: USA about 2,190; Canada about 1,580; Australia about 1,030; UK about 420; Chile about 180; Mexico about 160; Brazil about 70. No legend. No highlighted points; all bars the same red #EB483F, evenly spaced, each about 4.2% of slide width wide. No photographs, logos or icons.

**Design**

Background: Solid light grey #F1F1F1 with a white #FFFFFF band across the middle of the slide. Minimal, flat, editorial style. Background light grey #F1F1F1 for header and footer, white #FFFFFF for the chart band. Title in Photina-style serif regular, colour #545454, about 5.6% of slide height. Subtitle in the same serif, #545454, about 2.6% of slide height. Chart title and axis labels in Helvetica Neue (chart title bold, #545554, about 2.2% and 1.85% of slide height). Source line in Helvetica Neue regular #545454 about 1.85%. Footer presenter name in Helvetica Neue Bold #A6A6A6, date and slide number in Helvetica Neue regular #A6A6A6, about 1.85%. Accent colour is red #EB483F for bars only. Gridlines faint grey dotted, 1 px. No shadows, gradients, rounded corners or borders.

**Layout**

Full-width grey header band across the top holds the title left-aligned at about 20% from the left edge, with a smaller serif subtitle beneath it. A grey footer band at the bottom holds the source line left-aligned at x about 20.5% and the author, date and page number right-aligned near the right margin.

**Visuals**

Stacked area chart titled 'US advertising as % GDP', showing US advertising as a percentage of GDP from 1950 to 2019. Y axis runs 0.00% to 1.50% in 0.25% steps with faint dotted horizontal gridlines at 1.25%, 1.00% and 1.50%. X axis labelled with years 1950, 1960, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010, 2019. Five stacked series from bottom to top: TV (#DDDDDD, lightest grey), Radio (#A7A7A7), Newspapers (#424242, dark charcoal), Magazines (#686767), Internet (#EC473F, red, top layer). Total stack about 1.13% in 1950, peaking near 1.48% around 2000, falling to about 0.93% by 2019. Internet appears from about 1997 and rises to about 0.42% of GDP by 2000 before declining with the stack; by 2019 it spans roughly 0.53% to 0.93%, about 0.40% of GDP. TV is about 0.06% in 1950, about 0.52% at its 1986 high and about 0.32% in 2019. No individual printed data values are shown beyond axis ticks; the values above are estimates. Legend at upper left of chart listed top to bottom: Internet (red square), Magazines, Newspapers, Radio, TV (grey squares), with labels in dark grey. Internet is the highlighted series in red.

**Design**

Background: Light grey #F1F1F1 full-slide base with white #FFFFFF band from y 20.5% to 86.1%. Light grey #F1F1F1 header and footer bands framing a white #FFFFFF middle band. Title in a serif typeface resembling Photina (a Caslon-like serif), regular weight, colour #545454, at about 5.6% of slide height. Subtitle in the same serif, regular, #545454, about 2.6% of slide height. Chart label 'US advertising as % GDP' in Helvetica Neue Bold, #545554, about 2.2% of slide height. Axis labels and legend in Helvetica Neue regular, #535353 and #545554, about 1.85% of slide height. Source and footer text in Helvetica Neue, #545454 and #A6A6A6. Accent colour is red #EC473F used only for Internet. Area series have thin white separating outlines. No shadows or rounded corners.

Does ‘online advertising’ really exist? / Platforms give efficient proprietary targeting. **Layout**

Full-width three-band layout: a light grey header band (top 0 to 20.5%) holds the title and subtitle left-aligned at x 20.1%; a white middle band (20.5% to 86.1%) holds one horizontal stacked bar chart with its chart title left-aligned at x 20.5% and the value axis along the bottom; a light grey footer band (86.1% to 100%) holds the source line at left (x 20.5%) and the author, date and slide number at right, with the slide number right-aligned ending at about x 95.6%. Left margin about 20%, right margin about 4.5%. No logo.

**Visuals**

One horizontal stacked bar chart. Chart title: 'US online ad revenue, 2020 ($bn)'. Value axis: horizontal, labelled with ticks 0, 25, 50, 75, 100, 125 (units $bn, range 0 to 125), with thin dotted light grey vertical gridlines at each tick. Category axis: none printed; a thin solid grey vertical baseline at x 20.6%. Single bar (one row) spanning y 49.4% to 66.8%, divided into five segments in order left to right: Search Intent, about 55 (0 to about 55, #EB483F, red); Amazon Intent, about 14 (about 55 to about 69, #F0766F, coral); Facebook Interest, about 35 (about 69 to about 104, #F5A39F, light salmon); Next 5, about 5 (about 104 to about 109, #535353, dark grey); Other?, about 16 (about 109 to 125, #A7A7A7, mid grey). Values are estimates from bar lengths; the slide prints no numeric values for segments. No legend; segment names are printed inside the bars in white. Highlighted points: none. Segments separated by thin white hairlines.

**Design**

Background: Light grey #F1F1F1 full-bleed, with a white #FFFFFF band across the middle of the slide. Clean minimal consulting-style look. **Layout**

Full-width grey (#F1F1F1) header band holds the left-aligned title at top-left (x 20.1%) with a one-line serif subtitle beneath it, both starting on the same left edge. A white panel fills the middle band (y 20.5% to 86.1%) containing a single horizontal stacked bar chart with a bold chart title above it, category labels at the left, value axis along the bottom, and a grey footer band below holding a left-aligned source line and right-aligned author, date and page number.

**Visuals**

One horizontal stacked bar chart. Type: horizontal stacked bar chart. Title: 'US ad revenue, 2020 ($bn)', bold, top-left above the plot. X-axis: value axis 0 to 125, unit $bn (stated in the chart title), tick labels 0, 25, 50, 75, 100, 125 with faint dotted vertical gridlines at each tick running from about y 36% to 80%. Y-axis: two categories, Online (upper bar) and Offline (lower bar), labels right-aligned to the left of the axis; a thin solid grey vertical axis line at x about 20.6%. Series (estimates marked about, as the slide prints no values per segment): Online bar totals about 125 — Search about 55 (red #EB483F), Amazon about 14 (coral #F0766F), Facebook about 35 (light salmon #F5A39F), an unlabelled dark segment about 6 (#535353), and Other about 15 (grey #A7A7A7). Offline bar totals about 87 — TV about 54 (grey #A7A7A7), Print about 15 (dark grey #535353), Radio about 11 (mid grey #6A6A6A), and an unlabelled light segment about 7 (#DCDCDC). Labels are printed inside segments in white sans-serif text, with the Online and Offline labels printed only on the Search, Amazon, Facebook, TV, Print and Radio segments. No legend. No highlighted points. Segments separated by thin white borders. Online bar is in red and pink tones; Offline bar is in grey tones, so the two categories are colour-contrasted.

**Design**

Background of header and footer bands #F1F1F1 light grey with a white #FFFFFF chart panel. Title and subtitle in #545454 dark grey serif (Photina-style, regular weight, not bold). Chart title and category labels in #545454 bold/regular sans-serif (Helvetica Neue Bold for chart title, Helvetica Neue regular for labels). Body and source text in #545454 Helvetica Neue regular. Footer author name in bold #A6A6A6 grey, date and page number in regular #A6A6A6. Accent colours: red #EB483F for Search, graded pinks for Amazon and Facebook, greys for offline segments. Title about 5.6% of slide height, subtitle about 2.6%, chart labels and footer about 1.9% to 2.3%. Shapes are flat rectangles with no corner radius, no shadows, no gradients; gridlines are thin dotted grey lines.

Chart: stacked column chart titled Netflix subscribers (m), shown in bold sans-serif above the plot at top-left of the chart area. Y axis runs from 0 to 250 in steps of 50, with no axis unit label beyond the (m) in the title. Light dotted horizontal gridlines sit at each 50 step. **Layout**

Full-bleed light grey slide split into three horizontal bands: a grey header band across the top (about 0 to 20.5% of height) holding the title and subtitle, a white content band (about 20.5 to 86.1%) holding the chart, and a grey footer band (about 86.1 to 100%) holding the source line at left and the author, date and page number at right. Title and subtitle are left-aligned at about x 20.1%; the chart legend sits at the far left margin (x about 4.8%) and the chart plot runs to about x 94.6%; the source line aligns with the chart title at x about 20.5%; the page number sits at the right margin (x about 94.4%).

**Visuals**

One chart: a vertical stacked column chart titled 'Global electricity generation capacity'. Y axis: percentage from 0.0% to 10.0%, labelled at 0.0%, 2.5%, 5.0%, 7.5% and 10.0%, with light dotted horizontal gridlines at each labelled value. X axis: years 2010 to 2020, one column per year, with a thin grey baseline at 0.0%. Two stacked series: Wind (dark grey #535353, bottom segment) and Solar PV (red, top segment). Values are not printed on the slide; estimates read from the image (about values): Wind about 1.6% (2010), 2.0% (2011), 2.3% (2012), 2.8% (2013), 3.0% (2014), 3.4% (2015), 3.8% (2016), 4.4% (2017), 4.8% (2018), 5.0% (2019), 5.3% (2020). Total stack about 1.7% (2010), 2.2% (2011), 2.7% (2012), 3.3% (2013), 3.8% (2014), 4.4% (2015), 5.1% (2016), 6.1% (2017), 6.8% (2018), 7.3% (2019), 7.9% (2020); Solar PV segment is the difference, about 0.1% (2010) rising to about 2.6% (2020). Legend at upper left of the chart: red square labelled Solar PV above dark grey square labelled Wind. No series is highlighted. Columns are about 2.8% of slide width, with thin white separators between the two segments.

**Design**

Background light grey #F1F1F1 for header and footer bands, pure white #FFFFFF for the content band. Title in Photina-style serif (regular weight) in grey #545454, subtitle in the same serif in grey #545454. Chart title and chart text in Helvetica Neue style sans-serif; chart title bold #545554, axis labels regular #545454. Accent red about #EB4A3E for Solar PV; neutral dark grey #535353 for Wind. Footer author name in Helvetica Neue Bold #A6A6A6, date and page number in Helvetica Neue regular #A6A6A6, source line in Helvetica Neue regular #545454. Title is about 5.6% of slide height, subtitle and chart title about 2.6% and 2.2%, body and axis labels about 1.9%. Shapes are flat with no corner radius, shadows or gradients.

**Text**

**Layout**

A full-width grey header band (top 0 to about 20.5% of height) holds the title left-aligned at about 20% of slide width, with the subtitle beneath it. Below, a white content area (about 20.5% to 86%) holds one horizontal 100% stacked bar chart, with its chart title at top left and its x-axis labels beneath, starting at the same left edge as the title. A grey footer band (about 86% to 100%) holds 'Source: UN' at left and 'Benedict Evans — January 2021' with the page number 76 at right, aligned to the right margin at about 95%.

**Visuals**

One horizontal stacked bar chart. Chart title: 'Global greenhouse emissions, 2017'. X-axis: share of global greenhouse emissions, 0% to 100%, labelled at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 100%, with light dotted vertical gridlines at 25%, 50% and 75% and a solid grey vertical axis line at 0%. No y-axis labels. The bar sits centred vertically (about 49.4% to 66.8% of slide height) and spans the full axis from 0% to 100%. Segments left to right, with segment labels printed inside: Power generation (#EB483F red, label white, about 25%), Auto (#EB483F red, about 10%), Other transport (#F5A39F pale salmon, label white set vertically, about 4%), Agriculture (#535353 dark grey, about 24%), Buildings (#535353 dark grey, label white set vertically, about 6%), Industry (#535353 dark grey, about 21%), Other (#535353 dark grey, about 10%). Values are not printed on the slide; the segment widths above are estimates marked 'about'. Segments are separated by thin white vertical lines. Highlighted in red: Power generation and Auto; Other transport is a lighter red tint. No legend.

**Design**

Background: Solid light grey #F1F1F1 over the whole slide, with a white #FFFFFF band from about 20.5% to 86% of slide height. Light grey header and footer bands #F1F1F1 framing a white central panel #FFFFFF. Title in a serif face (PhotinaMT-like, regular weight) in grey #545454, large, about 5.6% of slide height for the title. Subtitle in the same serif, regular, about 2.6% of slide height, colour #545454. Chart title in HelveticaNeue-Bold sans-serif, about 2.2% of slide height, colour #545554. Segment labels in HelveticaNeue regular sans-serif, about 2.3% of slide height, white. Axis labels in HelveticaNeue regular, about 1.9%, colour #545554. Footer text in HelveticaNeue, about 1.9%; 'Benedict Evans' bold #A6A6A6 and the rest regular #A6A6A6. Accent colours: red #EB483F and pale red #F5A39F; bars dark grey #535353. Segments have square corners, no shadows, no gradients; thin white separators between segments; gridlines are thin dotted grey lines; axis line thin solid grey.

One photograph: a stack of four clear plastic clamshell trays of red plant-based burger patties, each tray holding two patties, arranged in a vertical stack of four packs viewed from the front at slightly elevated angle. Small yellow-green speckles decorate the teal sleeves. Lighting is soft and even studio lighting with faint shadows beneath the stack. Dominant colours are red patties, clear plastic, teal green #1FD6B0 approximately, black and white. The photograph is unboxed, placed on the light grey background with no border, with a soft fade at its bottom edge and no overlay or tint.

Title text is dark grey #545454 in a transitional serif (PhotinaMT, regular weight), set at roughly 5.6% of slide height per line with tight leading. Y axis: attendees (number of attendees, unlabelled units), range 0 to 15,000, gridlines dotted light grey at 2,500 intervals, labels 0, 2,500, 5,000, 7,500, 10,000, 12,500, 15,000. X axis: years 1985 to 2019, labels every five years from 1985 to 2015 (1985, 1990, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015), baseline solid grey. Six series, none with printed values, so values are estimates marked about: NeurIPS (solid red, darkest red) starts about 500 in 1995, about 2,000 in 2010, about 2,600 in 2014, about 5,200 in 2016, about 7,700 in 2017, about 8,000 in 2018 and about 13,500 in 2019, the highlighted endpoint. CVPR (solid light pink) starts about 1,200 in 2013 region, about 2,700 in 2015, about 3,600 in 2016, about 4,900 in 2017, about 6,500 in 2018 and about 9,200 in 2019. IJCAI (dashed grey) starts about 5,000 in 1985, falls to about 1,300 by 1997, runs about 1,000 to 1,500 through 2005 to 2013, then about 2,500 in 2018 and about 3,000 in 2019. AAAI (solid mid grey) starts about 4,400 in 1985, peaks about 5,400 in 1986, falls to about 1,400 in 1993, about 2,000 in 1994, about 1,300 in 1997, about 1,500 in 2004, about 1,100 in 2012, about 1,000 in 2014, about 1,800 in 2017, about 2,300 in 2018 and about 3,200 in 2019. IROS (solid red-orange) starts about 500 in 1995 region as a long flat line, rising to about 2,200 in 2016, about 2,700 in 2017, about 3,700 in 2018 and about 3,500 in 2019. ICML (solid salmon) starts about 400 in 2007, about 500 in 2008 to 2011, about 1,000 in 2014, about 1,800 in 2015, about 3,100 in 2016, about 2,400 in 2017, about 5,000 in 2018 and about 6,500 in 2019. Legend: vertical list at top-left of the chart, each entry a short line sample then label, in order NeurIPS, CVPR, IJCAI, AAAI, IROS, ICML. Line colours: NeurIPS and IROS in red tones, CVPR and ICML in pinks and salmons, IJCAI and AAAI in greys; the NeurIPS endpoint at 2019 is the most prominent point.

Background: Solid light grey #F1F1F1 covering the whole slide, with a white (#FFFFFF) band from about 20.5% to 86.1% of slide height. Light grey background (#F1F1F1) with a white central band for the chart. Title in a regular serif (Photina-style) at about 5.6% of slide height, dark grey #545454. ### Slide 80

**Text**

None of these people exist / These faces are algorithmically generated by a machine learning system / Source: ThisPersonDoesNotExist / Benedict Evans –– January 2021 / 80

**Layout**

Left-aligned title block at top with the title starting at about 20% from the left edge and the subtitle directly beneath it. A 4-column by 2-row grid of eight square face photographs fills the middle band, spanning about 20% to 75% of the width, with equal small gutters. The footer sits below the grid: source line at left under the first column, author, em dash and date at right, and the page number at far right. Left margin of the content is about 20%, right margin about 6%, with the left 20% of the slide empty.

**Visuals**

Eight square head-and-shoulders portrait photographs (1024 by 1024 pixels each) arranged in a 4 by 2 grid. Row 1, left to right: (1) a smiling man with short brown hair, showing upper teeth, wearing a dark grey-green collared shirt against a taupe-brown backdrop; (2) a man with dark wavy hair, closed-mouth slight smile, blue-grey collar, against a grey-brown backdrop; (3) a man with curly light-brown hair and thin wire-frame glasses, slight smile, dark jacket, against a blurred green and brown outdoor background; (4) a man with short dark hair, slight smile, dark blue collar, against a warm taupe backdrop. Row 2, left to right: (5) a balding man with grey-flecked stubble and beard, slight smile, dark shirt, against a brown backdrop; (6) a young girl with short dark hair, neutral expression with lips closed, light grey-white top, against a tan textured wall; (7) a man with short tousled brown hair, broad smile showing teeth, light grey collar, against a beige backdrop; (8) a smiling woman with long dark brown hair and bangs, pale skin, small earring, against a blurred green background. Lighting is soft, even and frontal on every face with no hard shadows. Framing is tight and centred with the eyes near the upper third; each portrait is cropped at the shoulders and sides, square and boxed, not full-bleed. No overlay or tint. Dominant colours across the grid are warm browns, taupes and greens with dark hair tones.

**Design**

Background: Solid light grey #F1F1F1 covering the whole slide. Plain light-grey background #F1F1F1 with no gradient or texture. Title in a light serif (PhotinaMT regular) coloured #545454, subtitle in the same serif at regular weight, #545454. Footer in Helvetica Neue regular #545454 for the source line, with the author name in Helvetica Neue Bold #A6A6A6 and the date and page number in Helvetica Neue regular #A6A6A6. Title cap height is roughly 5.6% of slide height, subtitle about 2.6%, footer about 1.9%. Photographs are square, butted with thin light-grey hairline gutters (about 0.1% of slide height) and no shadows, rounded corners or borders.

One line chart titled 'GDP (current price $tr)' in bold sans-serif. Y-axis: GDP in current-price trillions of US dollars, labelled 0 to 25 in steps of 5, with light dotted horizontal gridlines at each step. X-axis: years 1960 to 2019, labelled every decade from 1960 to 2010 plus 2019 at the right end, with a thin solid grey baseline at 0. Three series, each a continuous line about 0.3% of slide height thick with no markers: USA is dark grey (#545454) and rises from about 0.6 in 1960 to about 6 around 1990, about 10 around 2000, about 15 around 2010 and about 21.4 in 2019, with a small dip around 2009. Japan is light salmon-pink (#F4A6A6) and rises from about 0.1 in 1960 to about 1 around 1978, about 3 around 1988, a peak of about 5.5 around 1995, about 4 around 1998, about 5 around 2008, a peak of about 6.2 around 2012, then about 5 in 2013 and about 5.1 in 2019. China is red (#E8402F) and stays near 0 to about 0.5 until 1993, then rises to about 1.2 in 2000, about 4.8 around 2008, about 7.6 around 2011, about 10.5 around 2016, and about 14.3 in 2019, passing Japan around 2009. Legend at left: short line swatch followed by label, top to bottom: USA (dark grey), Japan (pink), China (red). No highlighted points or annotations.

**Layout**

Three equal-width horizontal bar charts in columns sit in a white band between a light grey title band at the top and a light grey footer band at the bottom. The title sits left-aligned at about 20% of slide width with its subtitle directly beneath, both starting at the same left edge as the source line. Chart column headings are bold and left-aligned above each chart; category labels are right-aligned in a column at the far left of the first chart, and 0% and 100% axis labels sit under each chart. The source line is bottom-left at the chart margin and the footer name, date and page number are bottom-right on the same baseline.

**Visuals**

Three 100% stacked horizontal bar charts sharing the same seven categories in the same row order: Solar, High-speed rail, Wind turbines, EVs, Robotics, Smartphones, Semiconductors. Each bar is a single track of 0% to 100% with a light grey #DDDDDD remainder and a dark or red share segment. Chart 1 'Chinese market share in China': dark #535353 share segments, about Solar 100%, High-speed rail 100%, Wind turbines about 80%, EVs about 95%, Robotics about 50%, Smartphones about 85%, Semiconductors about 2%; no values printed. Chart 2 'Market share outside China': dark #535353 segments, about Solar 50%, High-speed rail about 0.5%, Wind turbines about 5%, EVs about 5%, Robotics about 15%, Smartphones about 45%, Semiconductors 0%; no values printed. Chart 3 'Share of top-tier components from Chinese suppliers': red #EB483F segments, about Solar 75%, High-speed rail 80%, Wind turbines 70%, EVs 70%, Robotics 40%, Smartphones 25%, Semiconductors 5%; no values printed. Axes run 0% to 100% with a thin grey vertical baseline at 0% and a dotted grey gridline at 100%. No legend; the colour difference is explained by the headings only. No highlighted points.

**Design**

Background is light grey #F1F1F1 in the top and bottom bands with a pure white #FFFFFF middle band. Title is a large light-weight serif in dark grey #545454, subtitle is a smaller regular serif in the same grey. Chart headings and category names use a sans-serif (Helvetica Neue) in dark grey #545554, headings bold. Axis labels and source line are regular Helvetica Neue in #545454. Footer text is light grey #A6A6A6, name bold, date and page number regular. Bars are flat with no corner radius, no shadows and no gradients; bar height is about 3.5% of slide height with white hairline separators between bars. Title is about 5.6% of slide height, body and axis text about 1.9%.

The chart plot runs from about 17% to 95% of the width, with the legend in the left margin at about 5% and the title directly above the plot at about 20.5%. No slide-number box or logo, only the printed page number in the footer.

**Visuals**

One grouped vertical bar chart titled 'Chinese smartphone panel shipment share'. Y axis: percentage of shipments, 0% to 60%, gridlines every 10%, dotted light grey lines, labels 0% to 60%. X axis: years 2014 to 2019, categorical, no axis title. Two series per year: LCD (dark grey bars, printed as no values, estimated) and OLED (red bars, no values printed, estimated). Estimated LCD values: 2014 about 29%, 2015 about 29%, 2016 about 37%, 2017 about 42%, 2018 about 45%, 2019 about 52%. Estimated OLED values: 2014 about 0.5%, 2015 about 1%, 2016 about 1.5%, 2017 about 2%, 2018 about 5%, 2019 about 11%. Legend at upper left of chart: dark grey square labelled LCD above a red square labelled OLED. No highlighted points. Source attribution: IHS.

**Design**

Background: Light grey #F1F1F1 full-slide background, with a white #FFFFFF band from about 20.5% to 86% of the slide height. Light grey #F1F1F1 background for header and footer bands, pure white #FFFFFF middle band. Title in a serif display face (Photina-like, regular weight) in dark grey #545454, large at about 5.6% of slide height. Subtitle in the same serif, regular, about 2.6% of slide height, colour #545454. Chart title in bold Helvetica Neue style sans-serif, about 2.2% of slide height, colour #545554. Axis labels and legend in Helvetica Neue regular, about 1.85% of slide height, colour #545454. Footer text in Helvetica Neue, about 1.85%, with author name bold in #A6A6A6 and date and page number regular in #A6A6A6. Accent colour red #EE4B3F for OLED series; LCD bars #535353. Bars are flat with no outlines, no shadows, no gradients, square corners. Gridlines are thin dotted #A6A6A6-ish lines. Baseline is a thin solid grey line.

### Slide 96

**Text**

Meanwhile - a market with 1bn users / The end of the ‘American’ internet / Smartphone users, 2020 (m) / 1,000 / 750 / 500 / Western Europe / 250 / North America / 0 / China / RoW / Source: Apple, Google, CNNIC, @BenedictEvans / Benedict Evans / January 2021 / 96

**Layout**

Two-zone layout on a full-width grey (#F1F1F1) field: a grey header band holds the left-aligned title and subtitle starting at about 20% from the left edge, a white chart panel fills the middle from about 20.5% to 86% of the height, and a grey footer band holds the source line at left and the author, date and page number at right. The chart occupies the centre-right with a y-axis at about 17 to 19% and a bottom baseline at about 80% of the height; the page number sits at the far right of the footer at about 94% of the width.

**Visuals**

One bar chart, a stacked column chart. Title: Smartphone users, 2020 (m). Y-axis: 0 to 1,000 millions of users, labelled at 0, 250, 500, 750 and 1,000, with faint dotted horizontal gridlines at each label. X-axis categories: China and RoW. Series: China is a single solid red bar of about 940 (about, no value printed) in #EB483F, with no segment label. RoW is a stacked column of about 625 in total (about, no value printed): bottom segment North America, about 275 (about), dark grey #535353, labelled North America in white; top segment Western Europe, about 350 (about), mid grey #7F7F7F, labelled Western Europe in white. The two RoW segments are separated by a thin white line. No legend; series are identified by in-bar labels. No highlighted points beyond the red China bar, which is the only coloured element.

**Design**

Background light grey #F1F1F1 in the header and footer bands, with a white #FFFFFF chart panel between them. Title in PhotinaMT regular serif, #545454, about 5.6% of slide height. Subtitle in PhotinaMT regular serif, #545454, about 2.6%. Chart title in HelveticaNeue Bold sans-serif, #545554, about 2.2%. Axis labels, category labels and source line in HelveticaNeue regular sans-serif, #545554 or #545454, about 1.85%. Footer author name in HelveticaNeue Bold, #A6A6A6, about 1.85%; date and page number in HelveticaNeue regular, #A6A6A6. Accent colour is red #EB483F for China; RoW uses greys #7F7F7F and #535353. Bars are flat with no outlines, shadows or gradients; gridlines are thin dotted grey lines.

Benedict Evans —— January 2021

**Layout**

Two horizontal bands: a light grey header band (top 0 to about 20.5%) holding the title and subtitle left-aligned at x 20.1%, and a grey footer strip below a white middle band. The white band (about 20.5% to 86.1%) holds one bar chart spanning roughly x 18% to 96%; the chart title sits at top-left of the chart at x 20.5%, y 27.4%. Source line sits bottom-left at x 20.5%, y 90.9%; author, date and slide number sit bottom-right, the slide number at x 93.8%, y 91.1%, right margin about 4%.

**Visuals**

Vertical bar chart. Title: Facebook audience reach, 2020 (m). Y axis: unitless millions (m), range 0 to 300, gridlines at 0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, drawn as light grey dotted horizontal lines. X axis: country categories in descending order, baseline solid mid-grey line. Single series, bar values: India about 280 (printed value none, estimated); USA about 190; Indonesia about 130; Brazil about 120; Mexico about 85; Philipines about 72; Vietnam about 63; Thailand about 48; Egypt about 41; Bangladesh about 37; UK about 37. No values are printed on the bars. Colour highlighting: India, Indonesia, Brazil, Mexico, Philipines, Vietnam, Thailand, Egypt and Bangladesh are red bars; USA and UK are dark grey bars. No legend. Bars about 2.7% of slide width each, evenly spaced, with gaps of about 4%.

**Design**

Background: Light grey #F1F1F1 full-slide fill, with a white #FFFFFF band from about 20.5% to 86.1% of slide height behind the chart. Flat, minimal chart on light grey background. Title and subtitle in dark grey #545454 serif (PhotinaMT-style, Times-like). Chart title and axis labels in dark grey #545554 sans-serif (Helvetica Neue; chart title bold). Footer text in light grey #A6A6A6 sans-serif (Helvetica Neue; author name bold). Source line in #545454. Title is large, about 5.6% of slide height; subtitle about 2.6%; chart title, axis labels and footer about 1.9% to 2.2%. Accent colours: red #EB483F for highlighted bars, dark grey #535353 for the USA and UK bars. Gridlines light grey dotted, about 0.5pt. No shadows, gradients or rounded corners.

**Layout**

Two-band layout on a light grey field: a header band (top 20.5% of the slide) with the title and subtitle left-aligned at x 20.1%, and a white content band (y 20.5% to 86.1%) holding a full-width vertical grouped bar chart from x about 4.8% to 95.3%. The legend sits at the far left of the chart band (x 3.3%) above the plot. The footer sits on the grey band below the chart: source line left-aligned at x 20.5%, and author, date and page number right-aligned to x 95.3%. Title and subtitle share the x 20.1% left edge; the chart title and source line share the x 20.5% edge.

**Visuals**

Chart: grouped (clustered) vertical bar chart. Chart title printed above the plot: 'Mobile data consumption (EB/month)'. Y axis: 0 to 15 EB/month, tick labels 0, 5, 10, 15, with light dotted horizontal gridlines at 5, 10 and 15 and a solid grey baseline at 0. X axis: categories 2018, 2019, 2020, no axis title. Series (no values printed on the slide, so all values are estimates): China (red, #EB483F): 2018 about 5.9, 2019 about 10.2, 2020 about 13.2. India (pale pink, #FBDAD9): 2018 about 3.8, 2019 about 6.8, 2020 about 9.6. N American & W Europe (mid grey, #7F7F7F): 2018 about 4.3, 2019 about 5.9, 2020 about 8.4. Bars within each year are adjacent with thin white gaps between them, each about 5.5% of slide width, and the groups are evenly spaced. Legend: three entries stacked vertically at top left of the chart, each a small filled square followed by its label: China (red), India (pale pink), N American & W Europe (grey). No highlighted points. No logos, photographs or icons.

**Design**

Background light grey #F1F1F1 covering the whole slide, with a white content band from 20.5% to 86.1% of slide height. Title colour dark grey #545454 in a high-contrast serif (PhotinaMT regular), subtitle in the same serif and colour. Chart title and axis labels are dark grey #545554 in a Helvetica Neue style sans-serif; chart title in bold, tick and legend labels regular. Body and source text #545454 (legend labels #535353). Footer author name bold light grey #A6A6A6, date and page number regular #A6A6A6, all Helvetica Neue style sans-serif. Accent colours: China red #EB483F, India pale pink #FBDAD9, N American & W Europe grey #7F7F7F. Title is about 5.6% of slide height, subtitle about 2.6%, chart title and legend about 1.9% to 2.2%, footer text about 1.85%. Shapes are flat with no corner radii, shadows or gradients. Gridlines are thin dotted light grey lines; the baseline is a thin solid grey line.

Two series stacked: Consumer in red #EB483F at the bottom and Enterprise in pale pink #FBDAD9 on top; thin white separators between segments. Baseline is a thin grey solid line at 0.

**Design**

Background: Light grey #F1F1F1 full-slide fill with a white #FFFFFF band from y 20.5% to 86.1%. Two-tone grey and white layout with a title in a serif face (Photina-style, roman, regular weight, #545454) and chart and footer text in a Helvetica-style sans-serif (regular, with bold for the chart title and author name). ### Slide 112

**Text**

Where do you go to see the future?
‘The future is here, but it’s unevenly distributed’
1995 / Finland / Mobile
2000 / Japan / Mobile web
2010 / San Francisco / Smartphones
China? / India? / Brazil?
Benedict Evans — January 2021
112

**Layout**

Single-slide diagram layout on a full-bleed light grey field: title and italic-style subtitle are left-aligned at x≈20% starting at the top, with a horizontal row of four equal circles centred vertically in the lower-middle area, separated by arrows. Footer credit and page number sit bottom-right at about y 91%, right of centre, with the page number at the far right margin near x 94%.

**Visuals**

Diagram: a horizontal left-to-right process of four circles of equal size (each about 16.2% wide by 28.8% tall, diameter roughly equal) at x 19.4, 39.6, 59.7 and 79.8 percent, vertically at y 39.1%. The first three circles are dark grey #535353 and contain white text: '1995 / Finland / Mobile', '2000 / Japan / Mobile web', '2010 / San Francisco / Smartphones'. The fourth circle is red #EB483F and contains white text 'China? / India? / Brazil?'. Between each adjacent pair of circles is a solid light grey #BFBFBF right-pointing block arrow (about 4.0% wide by 10.4% tall, at y 48.4%, x 35.6, 55.7 and 75.8), with a notched chevron-style head and a rectangular shaft, not connected to the circles by lines. No photographs, logos or charts.

**Design**

Background very light grey #F1F1F1, flat with no gradient. Title in a Photina-style serif (Photina MT, regular weight) in dark grey #545454, roughly 5.6% of slide height for the capitals line. Subtitle in the same serif, regular, #545454, about 2.6% of slide height. Circle labels in Photina MT regular white #FFFFFF at about 3.0% of slide height, centred, three lines each with generous line spacing. Footer in Helvetica Neue: 'Benedict Evans' bold and the date and page number regular, all in light grey #A6A6A6 at about 1.9% of slide height. Shapes are flat with no shadows, no outlines, no rounded corners beyond the true circles.

### Slide 115

**Text**

Welcome to 2021 / Benedict Evans — January 2021 / 115

**Layout**

Single screenshot slide: the title sits top-left, left-aligned at about x 20% and y 5.5%, with the browser window image placed as a boxed figure at left-centre, about x 16.9% to 66.3% and y 14.9% to 95.5%. The footer sits bottom-right, with the author name and date on the left of the footer line and the page number at the far right, all on one baseline near y 91%. The right side of the slide is empty background.

**Visuals**

Screenshot of a Mac browser window (Safari-style) with traffic-light buttons at top left (red, yellow, green), a sidebar toggle and back/forward arrows, and an address bar reading 'twitter.com' with a padlock icon and reload icon. Window has a soft grey drop shadow and rounded corners. Inside, a Twitter-style left navigation column with the blue Twitter bird logo at top, then outline icons in a vertical stack: home (pentagon-style house with dot), search (magnifier), notifications (bell), messages (envelope), bookmarks (bookmark), lists (document lines), profile (person), more (circled dots), and a blue circular compose button with a quill/plus icon. The main column has a header with a blue back arrow and the bold word 'Profile'. Below is a pale blue-grey banner (#BFCDD5 approx.) spanning the column, with a large pale circular avatar placeholder (#F1F7F9 approx.) with a white ring overlapping the banner's bottom-left edge. Beneath is the bold handle '@realDonaldTrump'. A centred block reads 'Account suspended' in bold, with the smaller grey line 'Twitter suspends accounts which violate the Twitter Rules' where 'Twitter Rules' is in blue link colour. No photograph; the image is a flat, unshaded UI screenshot with no tint, cropped at the window edges only.

**Design**

Background light grey #F1F1F1. Title in a Photina-style book serif (Photina MT), regular weight, dark grey #545454, approximately 5.6% of slide height for the title cap-height region, sentence case. Footer in Helvetica Neue: author name bold and the rest regular, both mid grey #A6A6A6 at about 1.85% of slide height. No accent colour on the slide itself apart from the blue of the screenshot (#1DA1F2 approx.). Window has rounded corners of about 1% of width and a soft large drop shadow. A white rectangle sits behind the footer area at x 21.5%, y 78.1%, w 5.2%, h 9.3%, nearly invisible against the grey.

### Slide 120

**Text**

Every wave of tech changes the world, and gets regulated / Every important industry causes and expresses problems, and gets industry-specific regulation / Railways / Industrial / food / Aircraft, cars, / databases… / Internet / Benedict Evans –– January 2021 / 120

**Layout**

Single slide with no grid of columns: title and subtitle are left-aligned at x 20.1% starting at the top, leaving the left fifth of the slide empty. Four equal circles sit in a horizontal row across the middle of the slide, separated by three arrows, with the footer line (author, date, page number) bottom-right at y 91%.

**Visuals**

Four circles in a left-to-right process flow, joined by three right-pointing block arrows. Circle 1 (dark grey #535353): label 'Railways'. Circle 2 (dark grey #535353): label 'Industrial food'. Circle 3 (dark grey #535353): label 'Aircraft, cars, databases…'. Circle 4 (red #EB483F): label 'Internet', the only highlighted point. Each circle is about 16.2% of slide width and 28.8% of slide height, with white serif labels centred inside. Between circles are three light grey (#BFBFBF) block arrows with a rectangular shaft and triangular head, each about 6.5% wide and 9.6% high, vertically centred on the circles. No chart, table, photo or logo.

**Design**

Background: Solid light grey #F1F1F1 covering the whole slide. Flat background, no gradients or shadows. Title in PhotinaMT regular serif, colour #545454, about 5.6% of slide height. Subtitle in PhotinaMT regular serif, colour #545454, about 2.6% of slide height. Circle labels in PhotinaMT serif, white #FFFFFF, about 3.0% of slide height. Footer in HelveticaNeue sans-serif, #A6A6A6, about 1.9% of slide height, with 'Benedict Evans' bold. ### Slide 121

**Text**

But we don’t actually regulate ‘cars’ / Lots of different regulation for different issues and companies / ‘Regulate cars’ / Safety / Emissions / Supplier & / dealer / contracts / Drink driving / Speed limits / Parking & / congestion / Urban / planning / Public transit / And so much / more… / Benedict Evans / –– January 2021 / 121

**Layout**

Two-zone layout on a left-aligned margin. The title and subtitle sit top-left starting at about 20% of the slide width and 5.5% of the height. Below them, a red circle sits in the left-centre, a grey right arrow sits between it and a 3 by 3 grid of white rectangles on the right, which spans about 57.6% to 94.9% horizontally and 20.9% to 88.0% vertically. The footer line (Benedict Evans, date, page number) sits bottom-right at about 91% of the height, with the page number at the far right, about 94% across. Left margin about 20%, right margin about 5%.

**Visuals**

One red filled circle, centred at about x 30.5%, y 53.5%, diameter about 20.7% of width, with the white text ‘Regulate cars’ inside it. One grey right-pointing block arrow (solid #A7A7A7, flat, no outline) at x 46.5%, y 48.2%, w 5.2%, h 9.3%, placed between the circle and the grid. A 3 by 3 grid of rectangular tiles with a small gap between tiles (about 1.2% horizontal and 1.1% vertical): top row Safety, Emissions, Supplier & dealer contracts; middle row Drink driving, Speed limits, Parking & congestion; bottom row Urban planning, Public transit, And so much more… The eight tiles other than bottom-right are pure white #FFFFFF. The bottom-right tile has no separately measured fill and appears to match the slide background tone, so it reads as an unfilled tile. No photographs, logos, charts or icons.

**Design**

Background: Solid light grey #F1F1F1 covering the whole slide. Flat, minimal design on a light grey background. Titles and body text are dark grey #545454 in a regular-weight Photina MT serif (a Photina-style transitional serif with no italics), with the title set much larger than the subtitle and tile labels. Accent colour is red #EB483F for the circle; the arrow is mid-grey #A7A7A7. Tiles are plain white rectangles with square corners, no borders, no shadows. Footer is set in a small sans-serif (Helvetica Neue), with the name in bold and the date and page number in regular weight, all in light grey #A6A6A6. Title text size about 5.6% of slide height, subtitle and tile labels about 3.0%, footer about 1.9%.

### Slide 123

**Text**

This was not an antitrust problem
Car companies could reduce emissions, but they couldn’t build cycle lanes
Source: Cornelia Dinca
Benedict Evans — January 2021
123

**Layout**

Single content area on a light grey field: title and subtitle are left-aligned at the same left edge (about 20.1% of slide width) near the top, followed by a row of three equal-height photographs spanning roughly 20% to 95% of the width, with a source line at bottom left and footer credit and slide number at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Three photographs side by side in a row, each boxed with a thin soft drop shadow and square corners, all top-aligned and bottom-aligned. Left photo: black-and-white historical street scene of a long row of tall gabled, ornate brick-and-stone townhouses receding to a vanishing point on the right; pale overcast sky at top; in the street, men in dark suits and hats, women in long skirts, a horse-drawn cart and a few early motor cars, with a row of pedestrians on the pavement; a lamp post in the centre; tonal range is grey and sepia-neutral; cropped to a tall portrait frame. Middle photo: colour photograph (faded, muted) of a busy city street seen from above, with a dense queue of cars, vans, trucks and a white Volkswagen Beetle filling the carriageway with a dashed white lane line; brown-red tiled rooftops and tall brick buildings on both sides; hazy grey-beige sky with a church tower in the distance; pedestrians and a cyclist on the pavement; a traffic signal at the bottom edge; dominant colours are grey, beige and dull red; portrait crop. Right photo: bright colour photograph of a dense Amsterdam-style street with red-brick gabled houses on both sides, a church spire in the distance, a large crowd of cyclists, pedestrians and mopeds on a wide paved cycle lane, a yellow diamond warning sign in the lower right, parked bicycles along the right edge, a red LEICA sign and red awnings; pale blue sky; daylight, dominant colours red-brick, blue and white; portrait crop.

**Design**

Background is a flat light grey #F1F1F1 with no gradient or pattern. Title is a high-contrast serif (Photina-style, regular weight) in dark grey #545454, about 5.6% of slide height in cap-height terms. Subtitle is the same serif, regular, dark grey #545454, about 2.6% of slide height. Footer source line is a regular neo-grotesque sans (Helvetica Neue style) in dark grey #545454, about 1.9% of height. Footer credit name is Helvetica Neue Bold in light grey #A6A6A6 with the rest of the footer in Helvetica Neue regular #A6A6A6. Photographs have thin soft drop shadows and square corners; no rules or other shapes.

### Slide 124

**Text**

Pattern recognition
What happens when you regulate natural monopolies, or just sue them? It’s complicated
Mobile operators
Regulating MTRs &
roaming cut
earnings by ~25%
Broadband
LLU gave up to
half the market to
new entrants
Microsoft
“Lawsuits failed,
but slowed it down”
(Much disputed)
Regulate adtech?
Store commissions?
Wholesale access to
Google search data?
How many
lawsuits?
Benedict Evans — January 2021 124

**Layout**

Three equal columns of circles centred beneath a left-aligned title and subtitle, with the title block starting at about 20% from the left edge and the content area ending near 96% on the right. The title sits at the top-left at about 5.5% from the top, the subtitle directly beneath it, and a right-aligned footer with the author, date and slide number sits near the bottom right at about 91% from the top.

**Visuals**

Three identical white circles with thin red outlines arranged in a horizontal row, each containing a bold heading, a short body statement and, in the third circle, a bracketed note. Below each circle is a centred two-line question in the same serif. No photographs, icons, charts or logos. Circle 1 contains Mobile operators with Regulating MTRs & roaming cut earnings by ~25%, and is answered by Regulate adtech? / Store commissions?. Circle 2 contains Broadband with LLU gave up to half the market to new entrants, and is answered by Wholesale access to / Google search data?. Circle 3 contains Microsoft with “Lawsuits failed, but slowed it down” and (Much disputed), and is answered by How many / lawsuits?. X-axis: bank size bands in US dollars, from left to right '<$100m', '$100-250m', '$250-500m', '$500m-1bn', '$1bn-10bn'. Halfway to Europe between cocktails and coffee
Don't plan to catch up on your reading. There's too much to take in—too much to talk about on your first Jet Clipper* flight. While the stewardess removes the last cordial glass from your dinner table, she reminds you to set your watch five hours ahead and tells you that
there's barely enough time to finish a chapter before you see the lights of London. Pan Am Jets are fastest to London, the only Jets to Paris and Rome. And this summer, Pan Am is increasing its schedules to include as many as four Jet flights a day to Europe—with deluxe
President Special service available on every one. You can also fly economy-class Clipper Thrift service, if you wish, with fares starting as low as $453.60† round trip. For reservations, call your Travel Agent or any of Pan Am's 61 offices in the U. S. and Canada. *Trade-Mark, Reg. U.S. Pat. Off. †Fares subject to change.
World's Most Experienced Airline
Pan Am Jet Clippers…world's fastest airliners…the only economy-class Jet service…
the only Jets to all three capitals. London, Paris and Rome.
No other Jet to Europe offers you the extra comfort of Pan Am's exclusive first-class lounge.
Benedict Evans

**Layout**

Two-column split: a left text column starts at about 4.6% from the left edge with the title block sitting around 24% to 60% of the slide height, and a right-hand photograph occupies the full height from x 51.3% to 95.6%. **Visuals**

One vintage print advertisement, placed as a boxed, uncropped photograph on the right (1165 by 1600 pixels, full height of the slide, not full-bleed). It shows a 1950s Pan American airline print ad. Upper panel: a painted illustration of a first-class lounge cabin in a Boeing 707 with blue-grey walls and ceiling, ceiling lights, and a curved bulkhead with hot-air-balloon motifs. A uniformed pilot with captain's stripes and a cap under his arm stands at left; a stewardess in a blue uniform and cap carries a tray in the background; a man in a brown suit and a woman in a mustard-yellow dress holding a cigarette-like object sit or stand at centre; a girl in a red dress sits on a blue banquette at left; a man reads in a seat at right; a navy Pan Am suitcase with a globe logo sits on the floor at lower right. Lighting is soft and even, with dominant colours of blue-grey, mustard, red and brown. Caption in tiny type under the panel. Lower panel: white background with the bold headline, three columns of small serif body text, a tagline in italic, a small Pan Am globe logo on the tail of a stylised silver and white Boeing 707 with blue trim and 'PAN AMERICAN' along the fuselage, and the words 'World's Most Experienced Airline' at left. No overlays or tints.

**Layout**

Two-band header and footer on a light grey field with a white central panel holding a single full-width line chart. **Visuals**

One line chart titled 'US car travel', plotted on two y-axes against a shared year axis. Left axis: 'Bn miles', 0 to 4, gridlines at 1, 2, 3 and 4. Right axis: 'Deaths/bn miles (RH)', 0 to 300, labels at 0, 150 and 300. X-axis: years 1920 to 2020, labels every 20 years. Series 1, Bn miles (red line, left axis): about 0.09 in 1923, about 0.2 in 1930, about 0.7 in 1960, about 1.55 in 1978, about 2.1 in 1989, about 2.65 in 2000, about 3.2 in 2018. Series 2, Deaths/bn miles (dark grey line, right axis): about 216 in 1923, about 159 in 1930, about 113 in 1940, about 75 in 1950, about 54 in 1960, about 45 in 1970, about 35 in 1980, about 15 in 2000, about 12 in 2018. The two lines cross at about 1960. No values are printed on the slide; all values are estimates. Legend at top left of chart: red short line with 'Bn miles', dark grey short line with 'Deaths/bn miles (RH)'. No highlighted points. Gridlines are light grey dotted horizontal lines; the 0 baseline is a solid grey line.
